svg.title: $475,000 Operator Revenue to $190,000 Owner Profit
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-retained-revenue-waterfall; chart type: waterfall; title: $475,000 Operator Revenue to $190,000 Owner Profit; subtitle: Four expense deductions reconcile exactly to the Base-Case 40.0% net margin.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Annual USD. First and final bars are totals; intervening bars are signed deductions. Canonical revenue already excludes home face value and pass-through debt service. The four expense allocations are editorial assumptions totaling $285,000, not additional canonical inputs. Do not deduct senior debt twice.; caption: Conservative: $100,000 revenue less $72,000 expenses equals $28,000 profit at 28%. Base: $475,000 less $285,000 equals $190,000 at 40.0%. Scaled: $850,000 less $408,000 equals $442,000 at 52%. Core staffing is four people; scaled staffing is six. These are annual scenarios, not month-one run rates.; stages: label: Gross operator revenue; value: $475,000 annual retained-spread revenue before operating expenses; numeric value: 475000.0; detail: Illustratively, $210,000 earned net upfront spreads plus $265,000 retained annual wrap interest equals $475,000. Do not book every cash down payment as earned revenue. Apply transaction-specific accounting: interest follows applicable interest guidance, while any ASC 606 service component requires its own principal-versus-agent analysis.; label: Acquisition and closing expenses; value: Subtract $100,000 of annual direct transaction expenses; numeric value: -100000.0; detail: Allocate sourcing, title, recording, counsel, and transaction-specific origination expenses not already netted from upfront spreads. Running contribution becomes $375,000; property purchase principal is excluded.; label: Realized losses and carrying expenses; value: Subtract $80,000 of annual loss and workout expenses; numeric value: -80000.0; detail: Model recognized credit losses, property protection, workout counsel, and nonrecoverable carrying expenses. Running contribution becomes $295,000. Moving cash into a reserve account is not itself an expense.; label: Contractor and servicing expenses; value: Subtract $60,000 of annual recurring delivery expenses; numeric value: -60000.0; detail: Cover recurring contractor retainers, licensed servicing charges, reconciliation support, and borrower-service administration. Running contribution becomes $235,000; exclude origination charges already assigned above.; label: Systems and administrative overhead; value: Subtract $45,000 of annual recurring overhead expenses; numeric value: -45000.0; detail: Cover CRM, document controls, bookkeeping, business insurance, and administrative support. Combined with the prior $60,000, recurring overhead equals $105,000 annually, or $8,750 monthly, within the stated opex range.; label: Annual owner net profit; value: $190,000 remaining profit equals exactly 40.0% margin; numeric value: 190000.0; detail: Calculate $475,000 minus $100,000 minus $80,000 minus $60,000 minus $45,000. Owner distributions and personal taxes are outside this illustrative operating bridge; profit does not equal immediately distributable cash.

circle.title: label: Gross operator revenue; value: $475,000 annual retained-spread revenue before operating expenses; numeric value: 475000.0; detail: Illustratively, $210,000 earned net upfront spreads plus $265,000 retained annual wrap interest equals $475,000. Do not book every cash down payment as earned revenue. Apply transaction-specific accounting: interest follows applicable interest guidance, while any ASC 606 service component requires its own principal-versus-agent analysis.

label: Acquisition and closing expenses; value: Subtract $100,000 of annual direct transaction expenses; numeric value: -100000.0; detail: Allocate sourcing, title, recording, counsel, and transaction-specific origination expenses not already netted from upfront spreads. Running contribution becomes $375,000; property purchase principal is excluded.

label: Realized losses and carrying expenses; value: Subtract $80,000 of annual loss and workout expenses; numeric value: -80000.0; detail: Model recognized credit losses, property protection, workout counsel, and nonrecoverable carrying expenses. Running contribution becomes $295,000. Moving cash into a reserve account is not itself an expense.

label: Contractor and servicing expenses; value: Subtract $60,000 of annual recurring delivery expenses; numeric value: -60000.0; detail: Cover recurring contractor retainers, licensed servicing charges, reconciliation support, and borrower-service administration. Running contribution becomes $235,000; exclude origination charges already assigned above.

label: Systems and administrative overhead; value: Subtract $45,000 of annual recurring overhead expenses; numeric value: -45000.0; detail: Cover CRM, document controls, bookkeeping, business insurance, and administrative support. Combined with the prior $60,000, recurring overhead equals $105,000 annually, or $8,750 monthly, within the stated opex range.

label: Annual owner net profit; value: $190,000 remaining profit equals exactly 40.0% margin; numeric value: 190000.0; detail: Calculate $475,000 minus $100,000 minus $80,000 minus $60,000 minus $45,000. Owner distributions and personal taxes are outside this illustrative operating bridge; profit does not equal immediately distributable cash.

text.title: Assumptions: Annual USD. First and final bars are totals; intervening bars are signed deductions. Canonical revenue already excludes home face value and pass-through debt service. The four expense allocations are editorial assumptions totaling $285,000, not additional canonical inputs. Do not deduct senior debt twice.
